desc: Heartfelt stories of life's struggles and warm odes flush with double-meaning are offered across the most popular Regional Mexican music styles. Instrumentation & vocal phrasings for Banda, Corrido, Mariachi, Ranchera, and Tejano styles are featured.

tracks.desc: In this "good riddance" themed, Regional Mexican RANCHERA, the singer liberates himself from an unsatisfying relationship where he was always pegged as the villain. Happy to see her go, he is relieved to be free and uncaring of her future. Features violins, trumpets, guitarrón, vihuela, spanish nylon string guitar, accordion and six voices. Vocal uses include soap operas, human interest, courtroom & family dramas. Other alternate mix uses include travel, reality tv, lifestyle & cooking shows.

A Regional Mexican TEJANO style song about being an indisputable champion, where all who dare compete will be torn to pieces. Features drumset, spanish nylon string guitar, bajo quinto, accordion, bass and six voices. Vocal uses include car chases, auto racing, action scenes, relationship, family and crime dramas. Other alternate mix uses include uses include travel, documentaries, reality television, lifestyle programs, cooking shows, movies and series.

Alluding to the famous "Mary Jane", this double meaning, tongue in cheek Regional Mexican MARIACHI ode to beautiful ganja buds -- or love letter to a marvelous woman -- happily features violins, trumpets, guitarrón, spanish nylon string guitar, vihuela and six voices. Vocal uses include narco drama series, romance, relationships, soap operas, reality television, documentaries, crime and comedy scenes. Other alternate mix uses include travel, documentaries, lifestyle programs and cooking shows.

This passionate and bold Regional Mexican BANDA delivers a message on being the valiant and manly "black sheep" that everyone shuns socially but always counts on when there's trouble, or needs of help. Features tuba, spanish nylon string guitars, trumpets, trombones, clarinets, euphoniums, drumset and six voices. Vocal uses include crime, gang and narco dramas, political and protest themes, social critiques and activism. Other alt mix uses include marching, documentaries, politics and dramas.

Born to be happy! A "leave me be and let me live my life" Regional Mexican CORRIDO theme song that highlights individualistic notions of freedom. Features accordion, bajo quinto, bass, drumset and six voices. Vocal uses include nightlife dramas, party life, social critique, family issues, rebellion and personal freedom. Other alternate mix uses include celebrations, parties, lifestyle and cooking programs, travel documentaries and reality television.
